You are given one person (a thinker), the lead section of their encyclopedia article (EXTRACT), and a list of historical events and periods whose dates overlap the person's life (EVENTS, each with an id).

Say which of the listed events bear on this person, and how. Use only the EXTRACT: if the extract does not mention or clearly imply an event, do not connect it, even if you know the connection from elsewhere. An event that merely happened during the person's life is not a connection unless the extract brings it up.

For each connection give:
- "event": the id from the EVENTS list, exactly as written (Q followed by digits). Never an event that is not in the list.
- "type", one of:
  - "lived_through": the extract mentions the event as part of the person's circumstances, without saying they acted in it or wrote against it;
  - "took_part_in": the person acted in the event (fought, sat in the assembly, negotiated, signed, governed, led);
  - "wrote_in_response_to": a named work, or the person's writing generally, answers or treats the event; put the work's title in "work" if the extract names one;
  - "suffered_under": the person was exiled, imprisoned, censored, dismissed, persecuted or killed because of the event;
  - "shaped_by": the extract says the event formed the person's thinking, without naming a work.
- "reason": one sentence in your own words.
- "evidence": one sentence copied exactly from the EXTRACT, character for character, that supports the connection. Do not paraphrase, shorten or join sentences.
- "work": the title of the work, if the type is wrote_in_response_to and the extract names it; otherwise an empty string.

If an event in the list is the same thing under a broader or narrower name as one the extract mentions (the extract says "the civil war" and the list has "English Civil War"), connect it. If nothing in the extract bears on any listed event, return an empty list. Return JSON only, matching the schema you are given.

PERSON: Thomas Aquinas (1225–1274-03-14). Italian Dominican friar, philosopher, Catholic priest, and Doctor of the Church (1225–1274)

EXTRACT:
Thomas Aquinas (  ə-KWY-nəs; Italian: Tommaso d'Aquino, lit. 'Thomas of Aquino'; c. 1225 – 7 March 1274) was an Italian Dominican friar and priest, theologian, and philosopher. He is considered one of the most influential thinkers in the history of Catholic theology and Western philosophy. He is the father of a school of thought (encompassing both theology and philosophy) known as Thomism. 
A proponent of natural theology, Thomas argued that God is the source of the light of natural reason and the light of faith. He embraced several ideas put forward by Aristotle and sought to synthesize Aristotelian philosophy with the principles of Christianity. Among his best-known ideas include his Five Ways for proving the existence of God, his virtue ethics, and his sacramental theology. In addition to its vast influence on Catholic thought, his philosophy has influenced modern virtue ethics, aesthetics, and cognitive theory.
Thomas's best-known work is the unfinished Summa Theologica, or Summa Theologiae (1265–1274), which is a comprehensive guide to the theology of the Catholic Church. His body of work also includes the Disputed Questions on Truth (1256–1259), the Summa contra Gentiles (1259–1265), and numerous commentaries on Christian Scripture and on Aristotle. He is also known for his Eucharistic hymns, which form a part of the Church's liturgy. In 1323, nearly 50 years after his death, Thomas was canonized as a saint by Pope John XXII.
Thomas has been described as "the most influential thinker of the medieval period" and is generally considered to be one of the Catholic Church's greatest theologians and philosophers. As one of the 38 Doctors of the Church, he is known by multiple titles, including Doctor Angelicus ("Angelic Doctor"), Doctor Communis ("Universal Doctor"), and Doctor Humanitatis ("Doctor of Humanity").
